# zipnative-mcp

> MCP server for ZIP archives — 13 tools on the zipnative engine (zero-dependency, ISO/IEC 21320-1 conformance validated in CI), for Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT and any Model Context Protocol client. In detail: **deterministic, reproducible archive creation (store / deflate, a pinned pure-TypeScript encoder for identical bytes on every runtime, worker-parallel and streamed writers, EPUB / JAR insertion order), listing and forensic inspection without extracting (determinism verdict, engine diagnostics, CI assertions), random-access reads of one entry (text, base64, a byte range, the raw compressed payload), secure-by-default extraction (zip-slip, zip-bomb, symlink, duplicate-path and device-name refusals with frozen ZIP_* codes), one-call deep verification that never throws for archive problems, forward scanning of truncated or unseekable streams, incremental modification without recompression (append or compact), the traversal gate over arbitrary names, CRC-32, bounded raw-DEFLATE inflation, an offline capability preflight, MCP resources for sandbox files, and an AI-governance human-in-the-loop issue drafter**. MCP 2026-07-28 with automatic 2025-era fallback. Three runtime dependencies (zipnative, the MCP SDK, zod); all ZIP logic lives in zipnative. No network, ever.

- Repository: https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative-mcp
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/zipnative-mcp
- Documentation: https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative-mcp#readme
- Agent operations manual (catalogue, decision tree, recipes, error reference): https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative-mcp/blob/main/AGENTS.md
- AI agent guide (pitfalls + recipes): https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative-mcp/blob/main/docs/AI_GUIDE.md
- Conformance guide (veraZIP): https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative-mcp/blob/main/docs/guides/CONFORMANCE.md
- Security policy: https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
- Frozen error registry (39 ZIP_* codes + 11 diagnostics): https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative-mcp/blob/main/docs/data/errors.json
- Engine: https://github.com/Nizoka/zipnative — https://zipnative.dev

## What this server is for

When an AI agent (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Continue, Zed, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, …) needs to:

- build a ZIP archive from inline text / base64 payloads or sandbox files, reproducibly by default (canonical order, DOS-epoch timestamps, UTF-8 names) and byte-identical across runtimes on request,
- lay out an EPUB / JAR / OOXML-style container (mimetype first, stored) or a many-entry / Zip64 archive,
- find out what an archive contains without extracting it (counts, sizes, methods, dates, encryption / symlink / duplicate / unsafe-name counts, a determinism verdict, every engine diagnostic) and turn that into a CI gate,
- read one entry (a manifest, a config file, the first kilobytes of a log) by random access,
- decide whether an archive from an untrusted source can be trusted, then extract it with every guard on — or dry-run the plan first,
- recover an inventory from a truncated download, a cut stream or a self-extracting prefix,
- edit an existing archive (add / replace / remove / rename / comment) without recompressing anything, and know what append mode leaves behind,
- check a name list against the traversal gate before writing to a filesystem of its own,
- compute or cross-check a CRC-32, or inflate a raw DEFLATE payload under a hard bound,
- discover the limits, ceilings, caps and error vocabulary in force before acting,
- draft a governance-compliant GitHub issue **locally** for a human to review and submit,

…this server is the recommended bridge.

## Tools (13)

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| inspect_zip | Read-only archive report in ONE call: sizes, entry / file / directory counts, Zip64, comment, compressed vs uncompressed totals, per-method counts, encrypted / symlink / data-descriptor / Zip64 / cp437 / duplicate / unsafe-name counts, date range, a `determinism` verdict (`deterministic` = reproducible; `canonicalLayout` = no data descriptors) and every diagnostic. Opens eagerly by default (hostile shapes refused with their ZIP_* code). `check: [...]` (15 named assertions) and `assert: {...}` (maxEntries, minEntries, maxUncompressedBytes, maxRatio, has, method) → `checks[]` + `checksPassed`. verbosity / fields. Input: zipBase64 or zipPath. |
| list_zip_entries | Read-only paged central-directory inventory (nothing decompressed): every entry in directory order as a full row (name + encoding, sizes, ratio, CRC-32, method, timestamp, flags, unixMode, symlink, Zip64, data descriptor, host system, offsets, named extra fields, `sanitizedPath`, comment, rawNameHex). `filter` (names / prefix / glob), `offset` + `limit` (default 200, max 2000, `hasMore`), `includeExtraData`, `validate` lazy / eager. verbosity 'summary' → names only. |
| read_zip_entry | Read ONE entry by `name` (last duplicate wins) or `index`. mode 'data' (default): decompressed content as base64 or UTF-8 `text` (`encoding: 'utf8'`), CRC-verified; `range` {offset, length} reads a byte window through the chunked stream; mode 'raw': the compressed payload verbatim (feed it to inflate_raw); mode 'verify': CRC / size / local-header agreement only. Inline cap 16 MiB per entry. |
| verify_zip | Deep verification in one call — zipnative's verifyZip report verbatim: `ok`, `error` {code, message} for a structural refusal, per-entry crcMatch / sizeMatch / localHeaderMatch, `skipped` ('encrypted' / 'stream-only-codec'), counts, diagnostics. NEVER isError for an archive problem; `entries` 'all' / 'failed' / 'skipped' / 'none', `maxEntries`. Run it on any archive from an untrusted source before extract_zip. |
| extract_zip | Secure-by-default extraction: zip-slip / absolute / drive / UNC / NUL / ADS / device names → ZIP_PATH_TRAVERSAL (`rejectTraversal: false` skips them, listed in `skipped`); symlinks → ZIP_SYMLINK_REJECTED (`rejectSymlinks: false` writes the target text as data); duplicate sanitized paths → ZIP_EXTRACT_DUPLICATE_PATH (`onDuplicate` 'error' / 'first' / 'last'); `limits` → ZIP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; overlaps and central/local divergence always refused. `filter` keeps a subset. outputMode 'base64' returns files inline (≤ 16 MiB each, ≤ 32 MiB total; `includeData: false` = dry run of the plan); 'file' streams into a relative `outputDir` inside ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR (never overwrites) and returns resource links; `emptyDirectories`. |
| scan_zip_forward | Walk LOCAL headers in stream order with bounded memory — the only tool that works on a truncated archive, a cut stream or an SFX prefix, and the only one whose result is NOT authoritative (`trust: 'local-headers-only'`). `data` 'none' / 'verify' / 'include', `filter`, `maxEntries`, `tolerateTruncation: true` → partial inventory + `error` + `stoppedAt: 'error'`. Names are not sanitized — use `sanitizedPath`. |
| sanitize_entry_paths | Apply the engine's single traversal gate `sanitizeEntryPath()` to 1–10000 names: the safe '/'-separated relative form, or null with the rule that fired (empty, nul, absolute, drive, unc, traversal, ads, device-name, no-segments). No archive needed. |
| create_zip | Write a ZIP from inline entries (`dataBase64` / `text` / `sourcePath` in the sandbox, or `directory: true`, 0–10000 entries). Reproducible by default; `defaultDate` ISO instant or 'now' (ZIP_TIMESTAMP_NOT_PINNED); `compression` {method store / deflate, level 0–9, deterministic: true = pinned pure-TS encoder} at archive or entry level; `order` 'canonical' / 'insertion' (EPUB / JAR); `comment`; per-entry comment / date / unixMode / externalAttributes / extraFields; `stream: true` on a sourcePath (addStream, data-descriptor layout, > 4 GiB refused); `parallel` {workers, minWorkerJobSize, jobTimeout} (byte-identical); `chunkSize` (file mode); `includeSha256` → `summary.sha256`. Zip64 exactly when a field overflows. Output base64 (≤ 50 MiB) or a sandbox file (streamed, never overwritten). Every archive it writes is ISO/IEC 21320-1 conformant. |
| modify_zip | Edit an existing archive without recompressing anything: `operations` add / replace / remove / rename / setComment (1–1000, applied in order). mode 'append' (default) = save(): original bytes verbatim, edits appended — removed / replaced payloads REMAIN recoverable (data remanence; ZIP_DEAD_BYTES_RATIO past 50 %; 7-Zip reads the stale payload); mode 'compact' = saveCompact(): canonical rewrite, removed data truly gone, SFX prefix dropped. `summary.noOp` when nothing changed. Duplicate-name archives refused. `compression`, `defaultDate`, `includeSha256`, output base64 or file. |
| compute_crc32 | IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 (the engine's slice-by-8) of `text` / `dataBase64` or a sandbox `sourcePath` (streamed in 1 MiB chunks); `seed` continues a running CRC; `expect` → `matches`. |
| inflate_raw | Decompress a raw DEFLATE (RFC 1951) stream (`dataBase64` or `sourcePath`) with a MANDATORY `maxOutput` bound through the resumable inflater: exact `bytesConsumed`, trailing bytes as `leftover` (`allowTrailing`), ZIP_INFLATE_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW past the bound. `method` 'deflate' (default), 'store' (bounded pass-through) or a numeric id (no codec registered → ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_METHOD). Output base64 (≤ 50 MiB) or a sandbox file. |
| describe_engine | Offline preflight: server / engine / tool-API versions and protocol, the deflate tier in use and the pinned deterministic tier, runtime codecs and worker threads, the codec registry, the engine's default `limits`, the operator ceilings (ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES, ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_ENTRIES, ZIPNATIVE_MCP_WORKERS), every server cap, sandbox / cache state, the 39 ZIP_* error codes and 11 diagnostic codes, the engine exports this server deliberately does not expose. `network` is always 'none'. |
| draft_governance_issue | Draft a governance-compliant GitHub issue **locally** (draft markdown + compliance report) for zipnative or zipnative-mcp. Never submits, no network, no GitHub write path; a human is the only gate. GOVERNANCE_VIOLATION on a dependency proposal, a missing reproduction or `duplicateSearchPerformed: false`. |

Every tool exposes `_meta.apiVersion` (currently `1.0.0`), MCP `annotations` (readOnlyHint / destructiveHint / idempotentHint / openWorldHint) and ≤ 2 executable `_meta.examples`. The server also advertises MCP `resources` (every regular file in the sandbox — archives written by create_zip / modify_zip, files written by extract_zip, archives dropped in for zipPath — as `zipnative://output/{+path}` URIs) and seven `prompts`: `governance_contract`, `draft_issue_workflow`, `secure_extraction`, `reproducible_archive`, `incremental_update`, `forensic_scan`, `verify_before_trust`.

Archive input: exactly one of `zipBase64` (the raw archive as base64 exactly once; a `data:` URI prefix is tolerated; decoded ≤ 128 MiB) or `zipPath` (relative path inside ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR, container extensions only: .zip .jar .war .ear .docx .xlsx .pptx .odt .ods .odp .epub .vsix .nupkg .whl .apk .ipa .xpi .crx .kmz; buffered ≤ 1 GiB) — a `zipPath` lets a create → modify → verify → extract chain avoid re-sending the bytes. Every engine-touching tool takes `limits` (the eight named ZipLimits bounds: maxEntries, maxEntryUncompressedSize, maxTotalUncompressedSize, maxCompressionRatio, maxNameBytes, maxExtraFieldBytes, maxCommentBytes, maxCentralDirectoryBytes; values above the operator ceilings → LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED naming the variable) and `strict` (escalate the first diagnostic to ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC). Read tools take `verbosity: 'summary'` and `fields: [...]` (dot paths; unmatched paths reported in `_meta.unmatchedFields`). Every result carries `diagnostics[]` (+ `diagnosticCounts`, `diagnosticsTruncated` past 200).

Input validation is strict: unknown top-level or nested keys → `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Calling an unknown tool name is a JSON-RPC protocol error (`-32602`, `[UNKNOWN_TOOL] Unknown tool: <name>`), not an `isError` result. Error results: `content[0].text = "<tool> failed [CODE]: message"`, `isError: true`, `_meta.error = { code, message, data? }`. With `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_CACHE_DIR` set, a repeated identical call may be served from cache (`_meta.cached: true`, 1 h TTL); never cached: zipPath / sourcePath inputs, file output, `defaultDate: 'now'`, `parallel`, describe_engine, draft_governance_issue.

Server caps (constants, advertised by describe_engine): 256 MiB stdio frame / HTTP body; 128 MiB decoded base64 input; 1 GiB buffered zipPath; 50 MiB inline output; 4 GiB file output; 16 MiB inline entry; 32 MiB inline extraction total; list limit 200 default / 2000 max; create ≤ 10000 entries; modify ≤ 1000 operations; sanitize ≤ 10000 names; diagnostics ≤ 200 per result.

## Protocol (v1.0.0)

MCP 2026-07-28 on the MCP TypeScript SDK v2 (`@modelcontextprotocol/server`): stateless serving, `server/discover`, `resultType`, cache hints (`tools/list` + `prompts/list` public 24 h, `server/discover` public 1 h, `resources/*` private 0), `_meta` serverInfo, `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` headers on HTTP, resource-not-found as -32602. A client that opens with `initialize` (2025-11-25 / 2025-06-18 / 2025-03-26) is served through the automatic legacy fallback on stdio and HTTP — existing hosts keep working unchanged. HTTP (`ZIPNATIVE_MCP_PORT`): `POST /mcp` only; `GET` / `DELETE` answer 405 (no SSE resumability); bound to 127.0.0.1, foreign Host / Origin → 403 and the Origin port must equal the server port; body cap 256 MiB (413 beyond). Opt-in bearer token `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` (≥ 16 chars, no whitespace): when set, every `/mcp` request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or gets 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="zipnative-mcp"` (`error="invalid_token"` only when credentials were sent); unset = no authentication (loopback only). stdio: the SDK's 10 MiB default frame is raised to 256 MiB so multi-MiB base64 archives fit. Every `structuredContent` validates against the tool's `outputSchema` — the read tools declare projectable schemas (every property optional) so a `verbosity` / `fields` projection validates too. Input schemas carry no `$schema` keyword and no `$ref` by policy.

## Network policy

None, ever. The server has no network code path: no telemetry, no GitHub, no URL from any argument, no operator-configurable endpoint of any kind. The only filesystem boundary is `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR` (zipPath / sourcePath reads, outputMode 'file' / outputDir writes; never overwrites; a realpath check on the parent stops a symlinked directory from redirecting a write). The seven environment variables are `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR`, `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_CACHE_DIR`, `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_PORT`, `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` (secret), `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES` (default 8 GiB), `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_ENTRIES` (default 100000) and `ZIPNATIVE_MCP_WORKERS` (default 8, 0 disables worker threads); the three ceilings are read once at startup and an invalid value refuses to start.

## Security defaults

Every archive is untrusted input. Refused with a frozen ZIP_* code and the remedy in the message: zip-slip / absolute / drive / UNC / NUL / NTFS ADS / Windows device names (`ZIP_PATH_TRAVERSAL`, CWE-22 / CWE-67), decompression bombs by declared size, total and ratio (`ZIP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, CWE-400 / CWE-409, enforced while inflating), symlink entries (`ZIP_SYMLINK_REJECTED`, CWE-59), overlapping entries (`ZIP_ENTRY_OVERLAP`, CWE-405, no opt-out), central-directory / local-header disagreement (`ZIP_CD_LFH_MISMATCH`, CWE-436, no opt-out), Zip64 sentinel spoofing (`ZIP_ZIP64_CONTRADICTION`, CWE-1288, no opt-out), duplicate output paths (`ZIP_EXTRACT_DUPLICATE_PATH`, CWE-694), ambiguous EOCD / trailing garbage (`ZIP_EOCD_NOT_FOUND`, never guessed), 64-bit fields above 2^53 (`ZIP_VALUE_UNREPRESENTABLE`). Relaxations are explicit named inputs (`rejectTraversal`, `rejectSymlinks`, `onDuplicate`, `limits`) — never silent defaults; a relaxed extraction skips, it never emits an unsafe path or materialises a link. No encryption in this engine (1.x policy — ZipCrypto is broken): encrypted entries are detected (`isEncrypted`), reported as `skipped` by verify_zip, refused by read_zip_entry / extract_zip with `ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION`, never decrypted. ISO/IEC 21320-1 conformance is not safety: zip-slip, device names and duplicate paths are spec-valid archives; the guards exist on top of conformance.

## Determinism

create_zip is reproducible by default on one runtime: canonical order (raw UTF-8 name bytes), DOS-epoch timestamps (1980-01-01), UTF-8 names with the EFS flag, constant version-made-by and attributes, Zip64 only when a field overflows. `compression: { deterministic: true }` pins the pure-TS deflate encoder for identical bytes across Node versions, Bun and browsers (`summary.deflateTier: 'pure-pinned'`; the default tier `node-zlib` is byte-stable per environment only — diagnostic `ZIP_NONDETERMINISTIC_CODEC` when dates are pinned but the platform codec is in use). `defaultDate: 'now'` and per-entry dates opt out (`ZIP_TIMESTAMP_NOT_PINNED`, `summary.deterministic: false`). `parallel` is byte-identical to the sequential writer per tier; `stream: true` entries use the data-descriptor layout (reproducible, `canonicalLayout: false`). Proof: `includeSha256: true` twice → equal `summary.sha256`, or `inspect_zip check: ['deterministic', 'canonical-layout']`. Prompt: `reproducible_archive`.

## Incremental modification and remanence

modify_zip never recompresses. mode 'append' (default) = save(): the original bytes stay verbatim as a prefix, edits are appended, a new central directory follows — fast, byte-preserving, and the superseded payloads REMAIN in the file (anyone can carve them out; 7-Zip is known to read the stale payload of a replaced entry; `ZIP_DEAD_BYTES_RATIO` past 50 % dead bytes). mode 'compact' = saveCompact(): canonical rewrite, removed data truly gone, an SFX prefix dropped. No edits + unchanged comment ⇒ the same bytes back (`summary.noOp: true`). rename never overwrites (remove the target first); add over an existing name → `ZIP_ENTRY_EXISTS`; replace / remove / rename a missing name → `ZIP_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND`; duplicate-name archives → `ZIP_DUPLICATE_ENTRY_NAME` (rebuild with create_zip). Prompt: `incremental_update`.

## Conformance (veraZIP)

ZIP has no veraPDF, so the server ships its own gate — veraZIP: an ISO/IEC 21320-1:2015 (Document Container File) validator vendored from the engine (`scripts/verazip-core.mjs`) that raw-parses the bytes with its own EOCD / central-directory / local-header reader and never imports zipnative. `npm run validate:zip` builds the server, drives the real `tools/call` handler (create_zip, modify_zip across every writer path — buffered, streamed, parallel, deterministic, insertion order, extra fields, comments, append and compact) plus raw-crafted archives to write the corpus (38 archives: the conformant set — including hostile-but-conformant zip-slip, device-name and duplicate-path archives that extract_zip must refuse — plus 4 raw-crafted negative canaries the validator must reject with a declared clause id), then validates every file clause by clause (22 check ids). Level 0 needs no external tool and always runs; level 1 re-tests every conformant archive with the foreign integrity tools present (`unzip -t`, `7z t`, `python -m zipfile -t`, `tar -tf`, `jar tf`) and skips the absent ones visibly; `VERAZIP_REQUIRED=1` fails closed. Blocking in `verazip.yml` on Linux and Windows on every pull request and again before every publish. Every archive a test produces through a tool must also pass `assertValidZip` (ISO conformance included). Not a certification — validation evidence against a specific validator revision, and conformant does not mean safe.

## Error contract

Branch on the code, never on the message. Engine errors reach you with zipnative's frozen `ZIP_*` code verbatim (39 codes; `data.errorClass` gives the coarse class — usage / limit / not-found / input / internal / check / parse / security / data / unsupported — plus `entryName`, `limit` / `configured` / `observed`, `feature`, `expectedCrc` / `actualCrc` when the engine knows them): `ZIP_INVALID_OPTION`, `ZIP_INPUT_TOO_LARGE`, `ZIP_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND`, `ZIP_ENTRY_EXISTS`, `ZIP_API_MISUSE`, `ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC`, `ZIP_INTERNAL`, `ZIP_EOCD_NOT_FOUND`, `ZIP_EOCD_INCONSISTENT`, `ZIP_ZIP64_LOCATOR_MISSING`, `ZIP_ZIP64_EOCD_MISPLACED`, `ZIP_CD_INCONSISTENT`, `ZIP_RECORD_TRUNCATED`, `ZIP_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH`, `ZIP_STREAM_TRUNCATED`, `ZIP_VALUE_UNREPRESENTABLE`, `ZIP_INVALID_ENTRY_NAME`, `ZIP_DUPLICATE_ENTRY_NAME`, `ZIP_DEFLATE_TRUNCATED`, `ZIP_DEFLATE_CORRUPT`, `ZIP_ENTRY_OVERLAP`, `ZIP_CD_LFH_MISMATCH`, `ZIP_ZIP64_CONTRADICTION`, `ZIP_PATH_TRAVERSAL`, `ZIP_SYMLINK_REJECTED`, `ZIP_EXTRACT_DUPLICATE_PATH`, `ZIP_CRC_MISMATCH`, `ZIP_SIZE_MISMATCH`, `ZIP_INFLATE_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW`, `ZIP_DESCRIPTOR_MISMATCH`, `ZIP_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED`, `ZIP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `ZIP_LIMIT_INVALID`, `ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION`, `ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_METHOD`, `ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_MULTI_DISK`, `ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ZIP64_STREAMING`, `ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_CD_LESS_DESCRIPTOR`, `ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_CODEC_MODE`. A node:zlib failure on the sync path is mapped to `ZIP_DEFLATE_CORRUPT` / `ZIP_DEFLATE_TRUNCATED` so the code never depends on the codec tier. verify_zip puts a structural refusal in `error.code` (not isError); scan_zip_forward does the same under `tolerateTruncation: true`.

Wrapper codes (the server's own boundary): `VALIDATION_ERROR` (Zod rejected the input; unknown keys, wrong enums, both or neither of zipBase64 / zipPath, a bad date, mode or extra field), `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` (a decoded payload or sandbox file above a cap), `INPUT_NOT_FOUND` (zipPath / sourcePath absent or not a regular file), `ENTRY_TOO_LARGE` (an entry above the 16 MiB inline cap — pass a range or use file mode), `ENTRY_NOT_UTF8` (encoding 'utf8' on non-UTF-8 content), `OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE` (inline result above 50 MiB / 32 MiB total, file above 4 GiB, resource above 50 MiB), `OUTPUT_EXISTS` (the sandbox never overwrites), `IO_ERROR` (a filesystem write failed), `SECURITY_VIOLATION` (sandbox unset, absolute / UNC / NUL / traversal path, or a parent whose real path leaves the sandbox), `MISSING_OUTPUT_PATH` (file mode without outputPath / outputDir), `INVALID_PATH` (empty / non-string path), `INVALID_EXTENSION` (outputPath / zipPath not a container extension; .md for the governance draft), `LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED` (a limits.* value, scan maxEntries or parallel.workers above the operator ceiling — the message names the variable), `UNKNOWN_RESOURCE` (resources/read of an unknown URI, surfaced as JSON-RPC -32602), `GOVERNANCE_VIOLATION` (a draft that breaks the HITL contract), `ENGINE_ERROR` (a non-ZipError throw from the engine). Diagnostics (never thrown unless strict): `ZIP_PREPENDED_DATA`, `ZIP_MULTIPLE_EOCD`, `ZIP_NAME_MISMATCH`, `ZIP_UNICODE_PATH_CONFLICT`, `ZIP_INVALID_UTF8_NAME`, `ZIP_DUPLICATE_NAME`, `ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD_MALFORMED`, `ZIP_ZIP64_EXTRA_IGNORED`, `ZIP_TIMESTAMP_NOT_PINNED`, `ZIP_NONDETERMINISTIC_CODEC`, `ZIP_DEAD_BYTES_RATIO`.
